question.text: A bank with a net worth of Rs 400 Cr, CRAR of 12%, and net NPA of 2% applies to become a Trading Member on the currency derivatives segment. Based on the RBI-specified eligibility for AD Category I banks (net worth >= Rs 500 Cr, CRAR >= 10%, net NPA <= 3%, net profit in each of the last 3 years), what is the outcome?

answer.text: The bank is NOT eligible to become a TM on the currency derivatives segment because it fails the Rs 500 Cr net worth criterion, even though it satisfies the CRAR and NPA criteria
The bank is eligible because it meets the CRAR and NPA criteria; the net worth requirement is only Rs 100 Cr
The bank is eligible because RBI does not specify a minimum net worth for AD Category I banks on currency derivatives
The bank is eligible only if it also meets a Rs 3 Cr SEBI net worth norm

explanation.text: The Logic: For an AD Category I bank to become a TM on the currency derivatives segment, RBI requires net worth of at least Rs 500 Cr, CRAR of at least 10%, net NPA at or below 3%, and net profit in each of the last 3 years. This bank meets CRAR (12%) and NPA (2%) but fails the Rs 500 Cr net worth threshold with only Rs 400 Cr. Failing any single criterion makes the bank ineligible. The Trap: Confusing the SEBI equity derivatives TM net worth norms (which are decided by exchanges, not set as a fixed Rs 500 Cr) with the RBI-mandated currency derivatives norms. The audit flagged this because the original stem asked about both equity and currency segments, but the workbook does not establish equity TM eligibility from these facts; only the currency outcome is determinable. Note: The original item was ambiguous because it asked about both equity and currency derivatives but the facts provided only support a conclusion about currency derivatives. The stem has been narrowed to the currency derivatives segment so that the Rs 500 Cr / 10% CRAR / 3% NPA framework from NISM Series-I (December 2025), pp.199-206 uniquely determines the answer.
